title: Merged code/* branches leave the integration remote at merge, and the ones left from before are removed once from the operator's terminal
goal: The operator removes the code/* wildcard protection on the integration project, so the auto-merging request's remove_source_branch deletes the branch at merge (GitLab never deletes a protected source branch; 1379 merged code/* branches, all protected, on 2026-10-27); the next landed code item leaves no code/<id> head. The ones left from before go once, staged, run by the operator in a terminal: a read-only manifest (tip sha, the rule that admits it, merge request iid and state, item status; exclusions for an open or unmerged request, a tip pushed after the newest merged request, a tip not an ancestor of the integration main fetched at manifest time, merged under 24 h ago, a live claim or landing lock) with a dry-run summary and its sha256, then batches of at most 50 compare-and-delete pushes (git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/code/X:SHA origin :refs/heads/code/X), 5 s apart, stopping at the first unexpected rejection, logged to _cache/; recovery pushes a tip back from the manifest. No agent deletes a branch; kb/_self/git.md describes the retention and the cleanup. Evidence: reliability-authority-review.md BR-1 and section 7 item 12.

gates.question: How is the cause fixed: GitLab never deletes a protected code/* source branch at merge?
options: land deletes its own merged branch with compare-and-delete

gates.question: Has the operator removed the code/* protection and run the one-time staged cleanup from a terminal?
